THE SPLIT PLATE / RECIPE

100-Calorie Iced Protein Coffee

A five-minute iced coffee with 100 calories and 20g protein per glass. Blend the whey into a small coffee concentrate first for a smooth drink without visible clumps.

YIELD2 servings
TOTAL TIME5 min
COOK METHODSee method
EST. / SERVING~100 cal | ~20g protein
KEY TO SUCCESS: Blend whey into the CONCENTRATE first, before adding ice or milk. That's the whole point — mixing whey into cold milk directly = visible clumps that stay clumped.

Ingredients

CONCENTRATE (blend first)

  • 1 tbsp instant coffee (2 glass batch — 1/2 tbsp per glass)
  • 1 serving unflavored whey isolate (~28g protein — 2 glass batch, 1/2 serving per glass)
  • 4 tsp monk fruit / erythritol sweetener (2 glass batch — 2 tsp per glass)
  • 4-6 tbsp cold or room-temperature water (start with 4 tbsp, add up to 2 more if the concentrate needs help moving)

ASSEMBLY (per glass)

  • Ice, as needed
  • 1 cup fat-free ultra-filtered milk (2 glass batch — 1/2 cup per glass)

You want the caffeine hit of iced coffee AND a real protein serving in the same glass without a chalky shake or a Starbucks-drive-through calorie bomb. 100 cal / 20g protein per glass, 5 minutes end to end. The technique twist: whey blends into a small coffee concentrate BEFORE the milk goes in — that's why this doesn't taste like protein powder floating in coffee.

Method

  1. 1.ADD COFFEE. 1 tbsp instant coffee (or 1/2 tbsp per glass) into a tall blending cup.
  2. 2.ADD WHEY. 1 serving unflavored whey isolate. Series-standard whey — any clean-tasting unflavored isolate.
  3. 3.ADD SWEETENER. 4 tsp monk fruit / erythritol sweetener. Sweet enough to drink without adjusting; not sweet enough to read as dessert.
  4. 4.ADD WATER. Start with 4 tbsp cold or room-temp water. Reserve 2 more tbsp — add only if the concentrate needs help moving. Too much water weakens the finished coffee.
  5. 5.BLEND SMOOTH. Submerge the immersion-blender head BEFORE turning it on (splatter control). Blend until smooth, lightly foamy, zero visible clumps. This is the technique differentiator — whey dissolves into the concentrate now, so the finished drink doesn't taste chalky.
  6. 6.ADD ICE. Fill each glass with ice to the level you want.
  7. 7.ADD MILK. Pour 1/2 cup fat-free ultra-filtered milk over the ice in each glass.
  8. 8.STIR + SERVE. Stir thoroughly to combine the concentrate with the ice + milk. Serve immediately.

SPLIT PLATE SERVING

Adult: Serve the adult portion as described above.

Kid: Serve the kid portion as described above.

Keys to success

  • Start with 4 tbsp water. Add up to 2 more only if the concentrate needs help moving. Too much water = weak finished coffee.
  • Submerge the immersion-blender head BEFORE turning it on. Splatter control.

If something fails

Clumps in the finished drink: Whey wasn't blended into the concentrate long enough. Blend the coffee + whey + water combo for another 15-30 sec until zero visible clumps. Adding whey to cold milk directly = permanent clumps.

Drink tastes chalky: Same fix as clumps — under-blended concentrate. Also check the whey isolate brand: some are grittier than others. Isolate (not concentrate) blends smoother.

Coffee tastes weak: Too much water in the concentrate. Start with 4 tbsp; only add up to 2 more if the mix isn't blending smoothly. Also verify the instant coffee dose — 1/2 tbsp per glass is the minimum for real coffee flavor.

Drink is too sweet / not sweet enough: Monk fruit sweetener varies in intensity by brand. Start with 2 tsp per glass, taste after blend, adjust up to 3 tsp if needed. Add more sweetener to the concentrate before blending, not to the finished drink.

Splatter during blend: Submerge the immersion-blender head BEFORE turning it on. Use a taller cup. Blend from the bottom up.

Drink separates in the fridge: Whey isolate holds fine cold but the ice-melt dilutes the flavor over time. Best consumed fresh; hold up to 4-6 hours refrigerated (no ice yet) and add ice + milk at serving time.

Storage and reheating

Store: Best fresh. Concentrate (coffee + whey + water + sweetener blended smooth) holds 4-6 hours refrigerated in a sealed jar — add ice + milk at serving time.

Reheat: Don't — this is an iced drink. If you want a hot version, skip the ice and use warm (not boiling) milk. Boiling milk denatures the whey and creates chalky texture.

Lasts: Finished drink (with ice + milk) is best within 5-10 minutes. Ice dilutes the flavor over time. Concentrate alone holds 4-6 hours refrigerated.

Estimated nutrition

~100 cal | ~20g protein.

100 cal / 20g protein per glass (2 glasses per batch). Component breakdown per glass: 1/2 tbsp instant coffee (~2 cal / 0g protein) + 1/2 serving unflavored whey isolate (~55 cal / 14g protein — varies by brand) + 2 tsp monk fruit (~0 cal) + 3 tbsp water (0 cal) + 1/2 cup Fairlife fat-free (~45 cal / 6g protein) = ~102 cal / 20g protein raw sum. Rounds to the creator-provided 100 / 20 target. Marked estimated. Verify exact whey isolate + Fairlife labels before publishing as label-verified. Fat-free ultra-filtered milk is the macro-honesty unlock — 2% pushes to 130 cal / 20g protein per glass. Adult plate | Kid plate

Adult plate

Adult

Full recipe as written — 1 glass per adult at 100 cal / 20g protein. Second glass keeps in the fridge or serves a second adult.

Kid plate

Kid

Adult-only Powerup — this contains caffeine and is NOT a kid drink. Younger kids shouldn't have caffeine at all; older kids should get caffeine-free protein alternatives (a chocolate-milk-style whey shake or the Bone Broth Rice cross-recipe for a warm protein carrier).

Brands I use

Fairlife
Fat-Free Ultra-Filtered Milk (1/2 cup per glass)
Series-standard high-protein milk in the fat-free grade. 8g protein per 1/2 cup vs 4g in regular skim milk. 45 cal / 1/2 cup vs 40 cal skim — negligible cal delta for 2x the protein. Not sponsored.
Unflavored Whey Isolate
Any clean-tasting unflavored whey isolate — ~28g protein per serving
The protein spine. Isolate (not concentrate) blends smoother into the coffee concentrate. Splitting 1 serving across 2 glasses = ~14g whey protein per glass (~5-6g additional protein from the milk = ~20g total per glass).
Any Instant Coffee
Nescafé, Folgers, Trader Joe's Instant, etc. (1/2 tbsp per glass)
Caffeine spine. Instant blends into the concentrate without a coffeemaker step. Caffeine content varies by brand — check the package if caffeine intake matters.
Monk Fruit / Erythritol Sweetener
Lakanto Monk Fruit, Splenda Naturals, or any zero-cal blend (2 tsp per glass)
Zero-calorie sweetener that dissolves cleanly into the concentrate. Doesn't spike blood sugar. Any brand works — Lakanto is the mainstream reference.
